sentences.text: Shri Manmohan Joshi, learned counsel for the applicant.
Ms. Mamta Shandilya, learned counsel for the respondent/State.
Heard finally with the consent of the parties.
Unsuccessful applicant for getting relief from two Courts below has approached this Court by filing the present revision petition.
Facts of the case in brief are that on 09.09.2004 at about 7:20 in the morning, Food Inspector stopped the applicant who was going to sale milk and took a sample which was later found adulterated.
He was charge-sheeted and tried for the offence under Sections 7 (i) and 16 (1) (A) (I) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

After recording evidence, learned Trial Court held him guilty and awarded one year rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs.1500/- with default stipulation i.e. two months additional rigorous imprisonment in case of non-payment of fine.

Aggrieved by the order of the learned Trial Court, applicant filed revision petition before the Sessions Court but in its judgment dated 07.02.2018 passed in Criminal Appeal No.150/2016 the learned Sessions Judge upheld the conviction of the learned Trial Court but modified the sentence and awarded six months rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs.1500/-.
This order of the Appellate Court is under challenge in the present petition.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that he does not want to press the merits of the case.
He submits that the applicant belongs to a very poor family and is a small milk vendor.
He goes door to door to sale milk.
He is the only bread winner of the family and has two school going children and old aged parents fully dependent on him.
He does not has any other source of income.
His family does not HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH BENCH AT INDORE possess any agricultural land.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: His whole family is dependent on milk selling.
His business has got stuck and his family is facing serious financial crises due to his detention.

He is punished for the offence under sections 7(i)
read with 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
The milk found in his possession was not found unfit for human consumption or injurious to health.
The State Food Laboratory only opined that the sample taken from the applicant does not confirm the standard of fat.
In the sample 3.8% of fat was found against the standard fat of 4.5% minimum and solid fat was found 5.4% against the standard solid fat of 8.5% minimum.
No injuries to health substance like Urea, Neutraliser, Detergent etc were found in the sample.
The incident took place in the year 2004 and since then he is continuously facing the trial.
He has no criminal history and no other criminal Bheemsingh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 April, 2018

1 case of any type have been registered against him, therefore, a lenient view may be taken and his imprisonment may be condoned.
He is also ready to pay the enhanced fine amount.
Learned public prosecutor has not challenged the facts submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case as revealed from the record and submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant, I find that ends of justice would be achieved if the jail term of the applicant is reduced and find amount is enhanced to the reasonable extent.

In my considered opinion, looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, it would be just and proper if the jail term of the applicant is reduced to 3 months rigorous imprisonment with fine of Rs.5,000/-.
HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH BENCH AT INDORE

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH BENCH AT INDORE
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Consequently, the petition is partly allowed.

The conviction of the applicant for the offence under Sections 7(i) read with 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 is upheld, while he is awarded punishment of 3 months rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs.5,000/- in default of payment of fine he has to further undergo rigorous imprisonment for 1 month.
With the aforesaid modification, the present petition is allowed and disposed of.

(Virender Singh) Judge sourabh Date: 2018.04.06 10:24:21 +05'30'
